structure: High school course-based standards in tables, one table per standard. Course sections are headed 'HIGH SCHOOL - WORLD HISTORY I: ANCIENT TO MEDIEVAL' (earlier, before this range) and 'HIGH SCHOOL - WORLD HISTORY II: EARLY MODERN TO MODERN' (u7667), each with a course description, a 'Topics of Inquiry, Compelling Questions, and Standards' overview list (u7668, u7670), then 'Standards Tables' (u7672). Inquiry Topics N (N=1-8 for WH I, 1-7 for WH II) are headed 'Inquiry Topic N: <title> Compelling Question: <question>'. Each standard table has a code cell SSHS.WHI.n.m / SSHS.WHII.n.m with title, the standard statement ('Argue ...'), a 'Connections to the Rhode Island Anchor Standards' header with 12 anchor codes (CG.P, CG.RL, CG.RR, H.CC, H.HP, H.IG, G.HPE, G.HSP, G.WST, E.SA, E.PC, E.EG) and 'X' marks for the connected anchors, then 'Guiding Questions for Instruction' and 'Learning Assessment Objectives' cells. Table cells of the title/statement are split across lines in the extraction. Labeling: code, title, standard statement, anchor codes and X marks = standards; Guiding Questions and Learning Assessment Objectives = examples; all content is 9-12 (no grade-specific split).
